claim: the Workflows panel's Status/history feature correctly reports a chain's progress after a step retry
evidence: services/agent.py:chain_run_status()'s reset comparison used <= instead of <: _retry_chain_step() spawns a retry at the SAME chain_step as the failed attempt, and <= made a same-step retry indistinguishable from a genuine restart-from-zero, so the 'latest run' accumulator reset and discarded every earlier completed step -- reporting a fully-successful chain as still idle with a phantom pending first step. A second, related bug in the same function: the step-row lookup used next() over the un-reversed list, so even after fixing the reset it would have shown the ORIGINAL failed attempt instead of the retry's real (successful) outcome for the retried step.
fix_note: Changed <= to < in the reset comparison, and reversed the search order in the per-step row lookup so the most recent attempt wins. Probe: tests/gauntlet/test_workflow_chain_status_retry_reset.py (2 tests: the main bug, plus a no-op-shaped sanity check that a genuine restart-from-zero still resets correctly), proven red->green->red-on-revert.

evidence: routes/chat.py's /api/chat/send handler (chat_send, line ~1532-1540) builds the system prompt with provider='cloud' HARDCODED, before the router has run -- per _build_context_prompt's own docstring, provider='cloud' strips TIER_2/3 vault content unconditionally. _generate_agent then runs the SAME router /api/chat uses (including _route_vault()), which can correctly force provider:'local' for a vault-tier message -- but nothing re-assembles the prompt for the seat that actually got chosen. Net effect: no leak (vault content never reaches cloud, since it was already stripped), but the local seat that is ENTITLED to see full vault content gets a prompt that was redacted as if bound for the cloud -- a degraded/incomplete answer with no indication why. /api/chat already does this correctly (_prep_for(provider) at chat.py:730-736 defers prompt assembly until after routing, per chat.py:616) -- /api/chat/send just never got the same treatment. No UI caller found for /api/chat/send today (grepped index.html/app.html), but it is live, tested API surface (tests/api/test_chat_provenance.py, test_badge_truth.py).
queue_reason: Fix shape is clear (mirror /api/chat's defer-until-after-routing pattern) but requires restructuring chat_send's call order without breaking its other callers/tests, and severity is low (no UI exercises this endpoint today, and the failure mode is a worse answer, not a leak) -- lower priority than the fixes that landed this round, queued rather than rushed.

seam: router request to seat actually served
claim: a live voice session answers from the same seat text chat would use for an identical request
evidence: routes/voice.py called local_seats.resolve("reasoning") at two call sites (line 840 inside _local_brain_ready(), and ~line 1450 selecting the model for a live-voice reply) -- but "reasoning" is not a valid role token; it is the CAPABILITY that the role "brain" maps to (local_seats.py's _ROLE_TO_CAPABILITY). _configured("reasoning") returns None immediately (_ROLE_TO_CAPABILITY.get("reasoning") is None), so the user's actual configured orchestrator model (capability_routing.reasoning.model, the same setting routes/chat.py reads correctly for text chat) was never consulted for voice -- resolve() fell through to its size-ordered fallback and picked the SMALLEST installed local model unconditionally. claim: local-only mode covers the actual Gemini Live dispatch point (/ws/live), not just the advisory engine-selection recommendation
verdict: BROKEN, SEVERE, FIXED -- F16 was incomplete
evidence: F16 fixed local-only gating in _resolve_voice_engine (the advisory /api/voice/session-info recommendation) and _synthesize_tts_wav (TTS). Neither fix reached the actual /ws/live dispatch point (routes/voice.py:1592 ws_live): grep-confirmed ZERO reference to model_routing/local_only anywhere in its ~1300-line body before this fix. Its only gates were a WS token (opt-in, unset by default), password/session auth, and GEMINI_API_KEY presence -- once past those it unconditionally builds a Gemini client and streams mic audio/text/tool-results to it. Consequence: a stale browser tab that fetched session-info before local-only was turned on, or any client connecting to /ws/live directly (bypassing the recommendation), could still establish a real, unrestricted Gemini Live session in local-only mode -- the exact 'gate the recommendation, not the decision to send' defect class already documented 3-4x elsewhere in this audit (F9, F12, and F16 itself for the two paths it did fix).
fix_note: Added the same absolute local-only refusal ws_live's sibling paths already have, positioned before any Gemini key resolution/client work -- refuses with a clear error message rather than silently connecting. Probe: tests/gauntlet/test_ws_live_respects_local_only.py (source-level pin, the established pattern for this codebase's nested websocket closures per tests/unit/test_voice_live_tuning.py precedent -- checks the gate exists AND runs before Gemini key work, not just that the string appears somewhere). Proven red->green->red-on-revert.

claim: the voice websockets (/ws/voice-local, /ws/live) enforce the same fail-closed-when-unconfigured auth posture core.login_required() already established for HTTP routes
verdict: BROKEN, queued (security posture question, not mechanical)
evidence: core/__init__.py's login_required(): when _HTTP_AUTH_KEY is empty (no FRIDAY_PASSWORD/FRIDAY_REMOTE_KEY configured), a non-loopback caller is explicitly denied (403) -- fail-closed, per its own comment. Both voice websockets' inline auth blocks (routes/voice.py ~1179-1195 and ~1649-1656) instead gate on `if FRIDAY_PASSWORD and not session.get('authenticated') and not _loopback_trusted() and not _ui_tok_ok`. When FRIDAY_PASSWORD is empty, this whole condition short-circuits False and the block is skipped entirely -- NOT EVEN CHECKING _loopback_trusted() -- so the websocket accepts any connection unconditionally. Inert on the shipped default (server binds 127.0.0.1), but FRIDAY_BIND_HOST/FRIDAY_REMOTE_KEY are supported, documented knobs for remote/LAN access (memory: agent.friday HTTPS proxy work) -- a real, reachable configuration, not hypothetical.
queue_reason: This is an authentication-posture decision (should the WS auth check mirror login_required's fail-closed default exactly, potentially breaking same-machine voice for users who rely on the current fail-open-when-no-password behavior on a LAN-bound install?) rather than an obviously-safe mechanical fix -- touching auth logic on a live security boundary deserves Stephen's review of the exact before/after behavior, not an unattended overnight change.

claim: a federation SETTINGS_SYNC push only ever writes the sender's real, persisted settings -- never a transient in-memory overlay
evidence: routes/federation.py's SETTINGS_SYNC receive handler (~508-524) and the /api/federation/settings/sync send handler (~131-137) both build their delta from _load_settings() -- which returns _apply_offline_routing_overlay(_load_settings_raw()). That overlay's own docstring (core/__init__.py:2247-2254) states explicitly: 'Never persisted -- _save_settings writes from the file/the caller's delta, not from this overlaid dict.' Both federation call sites violate that invariant: model_routing (containing the overlay's transient mode:local_only/fallback_to_cloud:False when the sending device is offline) is in _SYNC_SAFE_KEYS and _DEEP_MERGED_BLOCKS, so it gets merged straight into the RECEIVING peer's persisted settings.json. A device that is WAN-offline but still LAN-reachable to a federation peer would silently and permanently rewrite that peer's real model_routing settings on any sync, and would itself broadcast its own transient offline state to every peer. No test in test_federation.py or tests/gauntlet/ exercises this.
queue_reason: Fix shape looks mechanical (use _load_settings_raw() instead of _load_settings() at both call sites) but this touches the federation trust/sync protocol's actual wire behavior between real peer devices -- queued rather than risking an unattended change to cross-device settings propagation without Stephen confirming _load_settings_raw() is really the intended fix and not a deeper protocol issue.

The UI's actual personality control is an unrelated free-text field saved through the main /api/settings POST. claim: every paid provider/tool Friday can call is metered by cost_meter
evidence: (a) ElevenLabs TTS (services/elevenlabs_tools.py:_tool_speak_text, line ~143-243) makes a real billed API call and even its own tool description says 'Costs characters against the ElevenLabs quota' -- yet has zero cost_meter references and no PRICING entries for its voice models. (b) Five entire opt-in provider catalogs -- Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Cohere (routing/provider_descriptors.py's BUILTIN_EXTRA_PROVIDERS) -- meter as exactly $0 for every call, structurally, through all three pricing-resolution tiers (cost_meter.PRICING has no entries for their models; their descriptors' cost_per_1k/pricing.static are empty by construction; their real /models endpoints don't return a pricing object for the generic discovery parser to capture). They share the exact same, already-verified-correct _call_openai -> cost_meter.meter() code path as every other openai-compatible provider (truncated responses meter correctly, confirmed this round) -- the code path works, the price table is just empty for these five. Disabled by default (need a user-supplied key), so inert until a user opts in -- but once they do, spend through these providers is invisible to the dashboard, budget alerts, and _rolling_spend() alike, with no error or indication anywhere.
queue_reason: Both need verified real per-model/per-character pricing from each provider's actual current pricing page before a number can be trusted in a real-money ledger -- this audit should not fabricate rates. Also fixed, low-risk and separate: added an explicit code comment to cost_meter.py stating Google Workspace API calls (Calendar/Gmail/Drive) are deliberately unmetered (personal-account volume sits under Google's free tier, not a paid tier) -- this seam's own check confirmed that assumption holds but found it was undocumented; the comment closes that documentation gap without any behavior change.

seam: settings write to settings read / onboarding copy
claim: the five built-in persona/distribution presets (default/journalist/developer/researcher/executive), shown during onboarding and in Settings > Distribution with descriptions like 'Code-heavy configuration with GitHub integration, CI/CD awareness, and dev tools', actually configure a differentiated workspace/layout/tool setup per persona
evidence: apply_distro() (services/distributions.py, reached live from /api/setup/complete during onboarding and /api/distros/<name>/apply from Settings) writes {distribution, show_all_workspaces, dock_layout} plus a personality override. dock_layout IS in DEFAULT_SETTINGS and IS written on every apply, but has ZERO readers anywhere in src/ or either HTML file -- grep-confirmed, round-trips through settings.json and does nothing. default_workspaces/default_providers/default_recipes are declared per-persona in BUILTIN_DISTROS but never even make it into apply_distro()'s delta -- read into Distribution.__init__ as attributes and never referenced again. show_all_workspaces is identically False across all five builtin distros, producing zero differentiation. The only field with a real effect is system_prompt_overrides.base_personality (a separate call). So the onboarding wizard's and Settings tab's persona descriptions promise curated workspaces/layout/tooling that never materializes beyond a system-prompt swap -- same defect class as F6/F14/F15 (a settings-shaped promise with no consumer) but arguably worse since this write path is live and prominently surfaced in onboarding, not merely dead UI.
queue_reason: Two different directions could resolve this, both outside this audit's mandate to decide alone: (a) build the actual differentiation (wire dock_layout to a real layout system, apply default_workspaces/providers/recipes on distro selection) -- substantial net-new feature work, not a mechanical wire-up; or (b) rewrite the onboarding/Settings copy to stop promising curated workspace/tooling differentiation it doesn't deliver -- user-facing copy, queues per Stephen's explicit carve-out. Flagging prominently given it's onboarding-facing, not a buried settings panel.

claim: a failing builtin scheduled task (news, weekly digest, memory dreaming, KG reindex, etc.) retries per a configured policy before giving up
verdict: BROKEN (as-shipped default, not a coding bug), queued
evidence: The retry mechanism itself is correctly implemented (dispatch()'s failure branch, scheduler.py:612-630, and _is_due()'s retry_pending priority check, scheduler.py:231-244, both correct and tested). But register_builtin_task() has no retry parameter, _seed_and_reconcile()'s seed record never sets one, and _normalize_record() fills the gap with {"max": 0, "backoff_seconds": 300} -- so EVERY builtin task ships with zero retry tolerance. attempts(1) <= maxr(0) is false on the very first failure, so any transient failure (a network blip, a momentarily-busy GPU) marks the job failed immediately and it silently waits until its next normal slot (next day/week/interval). No UI field exists to set retry.max/backoff_seconds on any schedule either.
queue_reason: Whether builtin jobs should get a default retry policy (and what policy -- how many attempts, what backoff) is a reliability-tuning decision, not a mechanical fix; a wrong default could also make a persistently-broken job retry needlessly for hours.

seam: settings write to settings read / child safety
claim: DEFAULT_SETTINGS' own documentation for minor_mode: 'When on, generation runs an age-appropriate filter ON TOP of the adult harm floor, and adult content is hidden in the gallery. This filters what the minor sees, not what exists.'
verdict: BROKEN -- the gallery-hiding half of this claim has NO implementation anywhere, HIGH PRIORITY (child safety)
evidence: minor_mode is genuinely changeable post-onboarding via a live Settings control in both HTML files, and the GENERATION-TIME half of the claim holds: creative_engine._minor_mode_active()/check_content_safety(), creative_policy.describe(), and music_engine's check_minor_appropriate path all re-read _load_settings() fresh on every generation call, so prompt-time content filtering correctly reflects the toggle at any time it's flipped. But grepped the entire repo for any gallery-side filtering keyed on minor_mode/is_adult/adult_content/nsfw/a rating tag on creation records: ZERO matches beyond the generation-time filters already covered. The creations-gallery list in both UI files filters only by file type and filename -- no adult/rating dimension exists on a creation record AT ALL, so there is nothing a gallery filter could even consult if one existed. Any adult-rated content generated before minor_mode was turned on (or by an adult user sharing the install) remains fully visible to a minor in the gallery after minor_mode is enabled. The documented behavior exists only in the settings-file comment, nowhere in code.

Building the actual gallery filter (adding a rating/adult tag to the creation record schema, then filtering the gallery list on it) is real feature work this audit should not attempt unattended and unverified for a safety-critical claim -- Stephen needs to see this first.

claim: local_preferred mode ('local first, cloud when it helps') is honored by TTS the same way it's honored by vision (routes/chat.py:369) and file-upload analysis (routes/core_routes.py:1085)
verdict: BROKEN (moderate, not severe -- local_only's absolute guarantee was untouched), FIXED
evidence: services/voice_engine.py:_synthesize_tts_wav()'s _prefer_local computation only checked (not core.GEMINI_API_KEY) or offline -- it never consulted model_routing.mode for local_preferred at all, so with a valid key and network up, TTS went straight to Gemini even in local_preferred mode, contradicting the mode's own documented definition and diverging from the established mode-check idiom used elsewhere in the same codebase. Probe: tests/gauntlet/test_tts_honors_local_preferred.py -- first draft of this probe had a real bug (a mock that raised to signal 'should not be called' was silently absorbed by the function's own broad except-and-fallback-to-local, making the test pass for the wrong reason even against unfixed code; rewritten to track calls in a list and assert after the call returns instead). Corrected probe proven red->green->red-on-revert.

claim: an MCP server subprocess's stdout/stderr cannot be used to grow Friday's memory unboundedly
evidence: MCPServerProcess._read_loop()/_drain_stderr() (mcp_client.py) iterated stdout/stderr via plain `for raw in proc.stdout:` -- Python's line iteration has no per-line size cap, so a malicious or buggy MCP server that never emits a newline (or sends one enormous JSON-RPC line) gets read into a single, unboundedly large Python string. The existing deque(maxlen=40) on _stderr_tail only bounds how many COMPLETED lines are retained, not the size of the one being assembled. Independent of and not mitigated by extension_security.gate_mcp_config()'s destructive-command scan, which checks what the launch command is, not what the running process later writes.
fix_note: Switched both loops to bounded readline(_MAX_LINE_CHARS) (16 MiB, generously larger than any real JSON-RPC message this protocol sends), discarding and resyncing on an oversized frame rather than materializing it. Probe: tests/gauntlet/test_mcp_stdio_line_size_bounded.py (a fake stdout stream distinguishing bounded readline() calls from unbounded bare iteration), proven red->green->red-on-revert.

seam: router request to seat actually served
claim: a background task's fallback attempt (when its primary local seat fails operationally) re-applies the same TIER-based content gating the primary attempt would have used for the seat it actually falls back to
evidence: services/agent.py's background-task path predicts a provider once (_predict_route_provider), builds the system prompt ONCE for that predicted provider via _build_context_prompt/vault_control.assemble_prompt (full TIER_2/3 content included for provider='local'), then hands that baked string to _generate_agent's fallback ladder. _generate_agent's own vault_access guard (a second, independent route() call) only blocks fallback when the MESSAGE itself is vault-forced -- not when the SYSTEM PROMPT was built assuming local. If a background task predicted local for an ordinary (non-vault-forced) reason and its primary attempt fails operationally (seat down, timeout), the ladder falls to a cloud leg reusing the untouched, fully-tiered system string -- sending TIER_2/3 personal context to a cloud provider with no re-gating. The identical predict-then-build-once-then-call-_generate_agent shape recurs at services/channels/manager.py, services/creative_pipeline.py's _exec_text_stage, and services/worker_adapters/claude_code_adapter.py -- 4 call sites share this exposure.
queue_reason: Distinct from F12 (already fixed as hardening) -- this one is reachable today, not merely structural. Fix shape needs a real design decision: either _generate_agent accepts a system-builder callback keyed by the actually-attempted provider (rebuild per leg), or fallback to cloud/openai gets blocked whenever the caller's OWN gating decision (not just the router's narrower vault_access) predicted local. Touches the core agentic dispatch loop used by every background task type -- queued rather than risking an unattended change here.

seam: router request to seat actually served
claim: Router.last_local_refusal is safe to read after a call under Flask's threaded=True concurrency
verdict: BROKEN (latent, currently inert), observed not fixed
evidence: last_local_refusal is unprotected, unlocked instance state on the process-wide Router singleton, written by _refuse() and read back into out['override_refused']. Two concurrent requests routing to local models can interleave: Thread A finishes computing its refusal-or-not, then before A reads self.last_local_refusal, Thread B's call overwrites the same attribute -- A's response can carry B's refusal reason or lose its own. grep confirms exactly one site reads out['override_refused'] anywhere in the codebase: the write itself -- nothing else consumes it (not chat.py, not agent.py, not either HTML file), so the race currently corrupts a value nobody uses.
note: Real race, zero observed impact today since nothing reads the corrupted field. Worth a queued fix (thread-local, or return-value-only) before anything gets wired to read it, but not urgent -- noted rather than fixed since it protects a currently-decorative value.

claim: cost metering has the same structural enforcement as egress/privacy gating (a single choke point every cloud call must pass through)
verdict: META-FINDING -- explains why 8+ separate unmetered-provider instances were found across 3 rounds
evidence: _seal_or_block (the egress/privacy choke point) is threaded through every outbound-cloud call site this audit has traced across every seam -- model_router.py, voice_engine.py, routes/voice.py, elevenlabs_tools.py, web_search.py, creative_engine.py -- a documented convention ('R3: one enforcement point for all providers', commented at model_router.py:171,991). cost_meter.meter()/record() has no equivalent requirement: it appears in only 8 files, ad hoc, call-site by call-site, and is conspicuously absent from that exact same list of voice/creative/elevenlabs/web-search sites that already have the egress seal. Every one of the ~8 unmetered instances found this session (Gemini TTS/Live, creative-gen images/video/music, Firecrawl/Brave, ElevenLabs, 5 provider catalogs) is explained by this one absence.
queue_reason: Higher-leverage than any individual gap: fixing this prevents the 9th/10th/11th instance rather than patching the ones already found. The durable fix isn't 'add meter() calls to N more files' but 'make outbound-cloud metering pass through a shared wrapper the way _seal_or_block already is' -- a design change, not something this audit should implement unilaterally.

claim: cost_meter.PRICING's USD assumption is safe for every provider that might ever get wired into it
verdict: BROKEN (latent trap, not yet triggered), observed not fixed
evidence: cost_meter.meter()'s _get(usage, 'cost') was built to detect OpenRouter's authoritative billed-USD field and trusts it as-is, no unit tag, no sanity bound. higgsfield_generate.py's _extract_credits() independently recognizes 'cost' as one of three field names the Higgsfield API uses for its CREDIT count -- a non-USD unit that only converts to USD via a plan-specific purchased-credit-pack rate not present anywhere in this repo. If Higgsfield generation is ever mechanically wired into cost_meter.meter() (the obvious next step for the already-queued unmetered-creative-gen gap, Q7) by passing its reply object straight through, the field-name collision would silently read Higgsfield credits as literal USD dollars.
note: Nothing currently connects the two subsystems, so this is not live yet -- flagged specifically so whoever picks up Q7's creative-gen metering work knows not to reach for the obvious 'just pass the reply object to meter()' shortcut for Higgsfield specifically.

claim: away_drain (the settings-gated background work-queue drain) is reachable/controllable by a user
verdict: BROKEN (feature appears incomplete, not a regression), observed not fixed
evidence: The read side is correctly wired end-to-end: away_drain_enabled() reads settings.away_drain.enabled (default False, 'takes the GPU'), and _tick() checks it before touching work_queue/gpu_headroom/the residency lease. But grepped the whole src/ tree and both HTML files for 'away_drain': the only hits are the DEFAULT_SETTINGS entry and the scheduler reader/tick -- no Settings UI checkbox anywhere, no API route that writes it, and away_drain_state() (whose own docstring says it exists 'so a scheduler that is off should be visibly off') has ZERO callers anywhere, not wired to any route either.
note: Unlike F1/F9/F14/etc., nothing in the product currently CLAIMS this is user-controllable -- it reads as an unfinished feature (backend built, UI never added) rather than a broken promise. Noted for completeness, not queued as urgent.

claim: forget_person.forget() durably removes a forgotten person from everything the KG will ever write going forward
evidence: indexer.py:437-456 and wiki_graph.py:434-455 both filter forgotten_names() against entity TITLE only, on every reindex -- a forgotten person's own titled node cannot resurface. But the filter never inspects entity DESCRIPTION text, and forget_person.forget()'s one-time prose-scrub only touches community_reports at the moment of forgetting, not future writes. If a later conversation mentions the forgotten person in relation to someone else (e.g. 'Bob's colleague Jane recommended the vendor'), a future nightly reindex can write 'Jane' straight into the surviving 'Bob' entity's description, untouched by any forgotten-name check.
queue_reason: This is privacy-relevant (a forget-me request not fully honored) but the correct fix isn't obviously safe to automate: scrubbing arbitrary free-text descriptions for a forgotten name risks false-positive matches corrupting unrelated content (a common name, a substring collision). Getting the matching precision right is a judgment call, not a mechanical wire-up.

claim: a correction to a fact is reflected in later KG retrieval, and the KG store's size is bounded/managed
evidence: (a) No invalidation-on-correction exists anywhere in this seam: delta-mode merges append a re-extracted entity's new description onto the old one (indexer.py:396-412) rather than replacing it, and conversation turns are treated as immutable/extract-once (never re-considered once indexed) -- so a correcting turn adds alongside the original stale fact rather than superseding it. The one path that would fully discard stale merged entities is mode='full', but no UI control anywhere ever sends mode:'full' (both call sites default to delta server-side). (b) The KG store (JSON artifacts + a dedicated ChromaDB collection) grows without bound for the life of an install -- grepped for prune/evict/ttl/retention, zero hits; the only size-related setting (max_visible_nodes) only truncates the /graph API's rendered response, never what gets persisted. Neither the docs nor the UI disclose this.
queue_reason: Both are real architectural gaps, not mechanical bugs: invalidation semantics (should a correction replace or merge? does tier matter?) and retention policy (what ages out, on what schedule, and is that itself a privacy question given some KG content is TIER_2/3) are product design decisions.

claim: the installer checks disk space against the actual model it is about to download before pulling multi-GB files
evidence: install.ps1 Step 1 (line 148-160) checks free disk against a flat $neededGb sized for the pip dependency tiers only -- never against the specific local model Step 2b/9 actually chooses to download. On the Python side, model_plan.plan() DOES compute a real disk_warning (model_plan.py:697-702, floor 10.0 GiB) and render() prints it -- but cli.py's cmd_models(install=True) prints the plan (warning included) and then unconditionally calls model_setup.install() regardless of disk_warning; model_setup.install() has no space check of its own. So a user whose recommended model needs e.g. 20.2GB but who has ~12-15GB free (enough to pass Step 1's flat 8GB floor) sees a printed warning line and the download proceeds anyway -- a full disk mid-pull fails confusingly deep inside 'ollama pull' rather than being caught up front.
queue_reason: The fix shape is clear (make cmd_models/model_setup.install() actually consult disk_warning before pulling) but it changes the installer's interactive UX -- a judgment call about whether to hard-abort, prompt for confirmation, or just warn more loudly is Stephen's to make, not mine.
